issues.summary: greenBeanFetchAllRows_ has an unbounded `while (true)` paging loop with no page cap and no guard that the offset advances. If a response carries paging.truncated:true + rowsIncluded:true with paging.returned === 0 (or a renamed/absent `returned`, which makes `offset += paging.returned` NaN), the identical UrlFetch is re-issued forever until the GAS 6-minute limit kills the trigger — hundreds of wasted fetch-quota calls, zero ingest, every Tuesday. The shopify.gs puller deleted in this same phase carried exactly this guard (SHOPIFY_MAX_PAGES = 50); it was dropped and not replaced. Tests cover the happy path, the size-guard abort and rowNumber dedup, but never a non-advancing page.

shopifyWeeklyPull_impl_ reads body.meta.weekStart and Number(body.summary.grossSales) with no shape validation — orderAppClassifyResponse_ only checks parsed.ok === true. Three failure modes, all money-affecting: (1) a 200 {ok:true} body missing `summary` throws a TypeError straight out of a scheduled trigger, contradicting orderAppFetch_'s documented 'never left to propagate' contract; (2) grossSales absent/null/non-numeric yields NaN or 0 written into the Summary `total` column while orderAppRunSuccess_ still stamps the heartbeat and raises no alert — and because NaN !== NaN, upsertRows_ then rewrites that row every single week while doGet serves the corrupt figure to the weekly report; (3) meta.weekStart is never checked against the requested weeks[i].label, so an API that ignores or clamps the `week` param writes one week four times (3 in-batch duplicatesSkipped) and still reports weeksFetched:4 with no apiFailed. Contrast greenBeanPull, which does surface upstream warnings/flags. No test covers a 200-ok body with an unexpected shape.

greenBeanInvoices_ accumulates `groups[k].total += line.totalCostIncGst` with no Number() coercion, unlike every other money read in the codebase (Number(body.summary.grossSales), Number(row.amount), Number(existingRow[2])). A string-typed totalCostIncGst makes the accumulator a string: 0 + '50' -> '050', then '050' + '25' -> '05025', and Math.round('05025' * 100) / 100 emits 5025 — a 100x overstated invoice, silently ingested into Suppliers and Summary with no flag and no alert. undefined yields a NaN total. The API's own `flags` mechanism exists precisely because 06_Stock_Intake cells can be non-numeric, so a numeric guarantee is not safe to assume here.

The resummarize loop discards weeklySummarize's return value and then unconditionally shrinks the queue to `remaining`, so a week that returned {refused:...} or an early `return;` is dropped from the queue as if it had been summarized, with nothing logged. Today every refusal path is excluded by construction (the incomplete-week guard in addAffectedWeek, ensureSheet having already created Suppliers, and withScriptLock_'s reentrancy depth), so this is latent rather than live — but the crash-safety design deliberately makes the queue the sole record of pending weeks, and this is the one path that can silently empty it.

'coffee_order_app' was removed from STALENESS_SOURCES on the stated grounds that it 'never stamps a heartbeat', but doPost stamps stalenessStampHeartbeat_(body.source) on every successful ingest (Code.gs:184) and kind:'revenue' from coffee_order_app is still explicitly sanctioned (docs/ingest-contract.md, tested at test_code.js:2699). Only the suppliers-kind shape was rejected. So the moment the Order app's wholesale-revenue POSTer ships, it stamps LAST_INGEST_coffee_order_app and sits unwatched, and testEveryHeartbeatSourceIsWatched cannot catch it because STAMPS_HEARTBEAT is a hand-maintained literal. Either re-add it, or make the exclusion conditional on there being no revenue writer.
